title: Musicals, concerts, drag shows: Where to catch a Dolly Parton tribute in the Twin Cities - NewsBreak
text:
By Dustin Nelson ,
12 hours ago There was never really any doubt, but the massive influence of Dolly Parton — as a musician, songwriter, artist, and philanthropist — has been apparent since her death on Aug. 25 at age 80.
Tributes have poured in from around the world for one of the most iconic American songwriters of any generation. (She had recently been named one of the 30 greatest living American songwriters by the New York Times; no surprise for someone who is supposed to have written “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You” on the day.)
For those looking to celebrate the life of the “Dumb Blonde” and “9 to 5” songwriter, multiple tribute events have sprung up around the Twin Cities.
That includes a performance that was not intended to be a tribute.
Dolly Parton Curtis Hilbun/Wikimedia Commons
Just hours before Parton’s death was made public, Hennepin Arts announced a performance of Dolly Parton’s Smoky Mountain Christmas Carol . The production, filled with Parton’s music, will stop at the State Theatre in Minneapolis on Nov. 24.
Meanwhile, First Avenue, along with interactive live music performers A Little Too Short to Be Stormtroopers, has announced a tribute concert on Jan. 8.
The organizers will be collecting children’s books at the event “to support Dolly’s mission of creating a love of books and reading.” Books will be donated to the local nonprofit The Free Book Buggie , a nod to the artist’s work through Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library.
Here are a few other Dolly-inspired events coming up around the Twin Cities:
Sept. 4 : A Night for Dolly at Aki’s BreadHaus and WunderBar in Minneapolis A happy hour with drink specials, dressing up like Parton, and music. Get $1 off a drink if you donate a book to Literacy Minnesota. Sept. 9 : Dolly Horror Picture Show at Bumbling Fools Mead in Minneapolis A drag tribute to Parton and actor Tim Curry, who also recently died, with a portion of ticket and drink proceeds going to The Dollywood Foundation. Sept. 16 : Queer Circus: Dolly & Tim – A Celebration Show at Can Can Wonderland in St. Paul Drag, live music, and trivia about Parton and Curry. March 19, 2027 : The Dolly Show at The Sheldon Theater in Red Wing
